extracted.intended_audience: university technology transfer offices, research administrators, contracts officers, and faculty involved in federally-funded research
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on rights, obligations, marking, and dissemination of technical data and computer software created under federal grants and contracts, summarizing agency-specific rules (NIH, NSF, DOD, DOE, NASA, EPA, USDA, DOT, etc.) and practical steps for universities to preserve IP and comply with funder requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Public Access Policy (manuscript submission timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH-funded investigators are requested to submit to PubMed Central an electronic version of the author’s final manuscript upon acceptance for publication. Authors are requested and strongly encouraged to specify posting of their final manuscripts for public accessibility as soon as possible and within twelve months of the publisher’s official date of final publication; the publication date is the publisher’s official date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reservation of rights by grantees/investigators in assignment agreements with journal publishers may be necessary to comply. This policy replaced the proposed six-month delay with a more flexible timing up to 12 months and stresses early posting when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF dissemination and data-sharing expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF expects investigators to promptly prepare and submit for publication significant findings with accurate authorship, and to share primary data, samples, physical collections, and other supporting materials with other researchers at no more than incremental cost and within a reasonable time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators should permit and encourage publication by those performing the work unless the grantee intends to publish themselves. Privileged or confidential information should be released only in forms that protect privacy. NSF encourages sharing of software and inventions to make them widely available and usable. See GPM Section 734 and FDP Article 14.a.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF copyright clause and government license
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise specified, the grantee may own or permit others to own copyright in subject writings, but if the grantee (or others) own copyright, the federal government will have a nonexclusive, nontransferable, irrevocable, royalty-free license to exercise or have exercised for or on behalf of the U.S. throughout the world all the exclusive rights provided by copyright.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF normally acquires only rights needed to achieve its purposes or to comply with government-wide policies; special copyright provisions may be negotiated for particular situations (e.g., international agreements).

rubrics_metrics.name: DOD rights in data and government-purpose license
rubrics_metrics.description: Under DODGARS (following OMB A-110 §36), the recipient may copyright work developed under an award, but DOD components reserve a royalty-free, nonexclusive, and irrevocable right to reproduce, publish, or otherwise use the work for federal purposes and to authorize others to do so. The federal government has the right to obtain, reproduce, publish, or otherwise use data first produced under an award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOD defines research data for these purposes and implements Shelby Amendment provisions. Many DOD research agencies participate in FDP but may have agency-specific applications of the general terms and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to affix appropriate markings to data delivered to the government
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions are responsible for affixing appropriate notices/legends identifying government rights on all technical data and computer software delivered under grants or contracts; if restricted data/software are not properly marked in accordance with agency regulations, the government by default obtains unlimited rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorrect or absent markings can result in the government ignoring or cancelling markings, returning deliverables as nonacceptable, allowing remarking at contractor expense, or obtaining unlimited rights. Universities should educate faculty and research staff and adopt consistent marking procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: DFARS prescriptive marking, recordkeeping, and procedures (DOD)
rubrics_metrics.description: DFARS requires mandatory, prescriptive marking for all restricted technical data and software delivered to DOD, including use of one of four allowed markings corresponding to government purpose rights, limited rights, special license rights, and copyright notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractors must maintain written records sufficient to justify restrictive markings, have written procedures assuring restrictive markings are used only when authorized, and identify deliverable restricted data in contract attachments. Legends must include the government rights identification, contract number, contractor name/address, expiration date of restrictive rights, and a definition of the rights/restrictions; place legends on transmittal documents, storage containers, and each page; highlight/identify restricted portions; electronic transmissions must also contain a notice. Universities are advised to incorporate DFARS standards into internal policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAR marking requirements and consequences (civilian agencies / contracts)
rubrics_metrics.description: FAR clauses prescribe the content of limited or restricted rights legends (e.g., notice that government may reproduce for government purposes only and not use for manufacturing or disclose outside government) but are generally silent on where to place the notice (per-page, first page, packaging, etc.). If data/software are delivered without the legend or copyright notice where appropriate, FAR presumes the contractor provided the government with unlimited rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The government may ignore, cancel, or return incorrect markings or permit remarking at contractor expense. Because FAR provides less placement guidance than DFARS, universities are recommended to adopt DFARS-style practices to avoid loss of rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOE expanded rights approach and use of procurement-style clauses in assistance awards
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE applies procurement-style terms to assistance awards, migrating its approach from contracts to grants, thereby giving DOE broader patent and data rights than other federal agencies; DOE requires use of Alternate V of FAR 52.227-14 (and related clauses) and inserts DOE-specific amendments (e.g., 48 CFR 927-409) into grant terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although universities may establish copyright in data first produced under DOE awards, DOE’s assistance regulations expand agency rights in pre-grant (proposal) and post-grant areas (e.g., 'Unlimited Rights in Proposal Data' and 'Additional Technical Data'), and solicitations must include representations of limited rights data and restricted computer software at 52.227-15. Grantees should expect DOE to treat data rights more like procurement matters and consult DEAR/FAR/48 CFR 927.4 guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOE Alternate VI license and limited circumstances to avoid licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE Alternate VI gives the government (or a third party on its behalf) authority to require license rights to proprietary contract data unless the contractor demonstrates certain exceptions (data not essential to design/fabrication, commercially competitive alternative, data already supplied sufficiently, or data obtainable from another firm).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are few circumstances under which the contractor will not have to provide the government with a nonexclusive license; this is particularly relevant when subcontracting or collaborating with industry partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency adherence to OMB Circular A-110 (NASA, EPA, Department of Education, NEA/NEH, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many civilian agencies follow OMB Circular A-110: recipients may assert copyright in works developed under awards, but the government receives a royalty-free, nonexclusive, irrevocable license to reproduce, publish, or otherwise use the work for federal purposes and to authorize others to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency-specific nuances exist: EPA requires copies of peer-reviewed journal articles to be provided to EPA and specific acknowledgments; NEH/NEA clarify 'federal purposes' and emphasize not interfering with grantee commercialization; NASA/EPA generally do not have additional FDP-specific RITD conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: CSREES/USDA GenBank submission requirement for genome sequence data
rubrics_metrics.description: CSREES requires that genome sequence data obtained under awards be submitted to GenBank, and the date of submission must be the same date as the government’s right to publish as indicated in the award terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission to GenBank is without charge; follow NCBI/GenBank protocols. CSREES is an FDP member and its agency-specific conditions contain a similar requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOT property trust relationship for grant-acquired property
rubrics_metrics.description: DOT grant regulations include a property trust relationship providing that property (including intangible property) acquired or improved with federal funds must be held in trust by the recipient as trustee for the beneficiaries of the project or program; DOT may require recording liens or notices to indicate federal acquisition and applicable use/disposition conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 49 CFR Part 19 and DOT grant terms; DOT does not participate in FDP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant marking practices and publication acknowledgments (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Most grant guidelines are silent on marking and protection of data/software, because granting agencies primarily seek dissemination; however, institutions must identify data/software created under sponsored programs, correctly mark any restricted rights data delivered to the government, and follow agency publication acknowledgment/disclaimer requirements (e.g., NSF acknowledgment: 'This material is based on work supported by the National Science Foundation under Grant No.___' and disclaimers for non-journal publications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unmarked data/software delivered to the government typically results in an unlimited license to the government. Using DFARS marking practices can help institutions preserve rights when deliverables are required under grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability for inclusion of third-party copyrighted material in deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE (and other agencies) impose liabilities on grantees and contractors for knowingly including material copyrighted by others in any written material furnished or delivered under an award without obtaining appropriate licenses or approvals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions must ensure proper clearances for third-party copyrighted material used in grant deliverables to avoid liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical recommendation: develop institutional marking policies and negotiation attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Universities should develop written policies/procedures explaining requirements and processes for marking and protecting technical data and software, ensure during negotiations that restricted deliverables are identified in contract attachments, and maintain records justifying restrictive markings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A written institutional policy aids education of faculty/staff, ensures compliance with DFARS/FAR/agency rules, and allows negotiation of modifications if additional restricted deliverables arise during a project (e.g., by using special forms to modify attachments).
